races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Steve Donoghue Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Penfolds Grange
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer partnered by Oisin Murphy, whose course-craft at Epsom is a genuine asset; 50 days between runs is worth monitoring, but two placed efforts at this trip on similar ground suggest the distance is not an issue, and this horse has upside if the run of the race falls kindly in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Penfolds Grange has been largely consistent, with two seconds and a third among his last five starts, but remains without a win in that sequence. Back from a 50-day break carrying 142lb from stall eight, our rating puts him firmly among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Kitaro Kich
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for George Baker, whose trainer has had one winner from fifteen in the past fortnight; the switch to a tongue tie is noted, and three runs on good ground in recent history give some confidence on the surface, though the step up to ten furlongs-plus on this profile is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Kitaro Kich won three starts back and, despite an underwhelming sixth next time, rallied to a fourth last time out. Fourteen days on from that run, carrying 141lb from stall one, our top rating of 77 marks him the biggest threat in this field.

runners_data.name: Eutropia
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's yard is in decent form (2 from 8, 14-day window) and this mare has winning form at a mile and a quarter, with her two victories on firmer ground relevant here; Tom Marquand takes over in the saddle, and a third placing on good earlier this term keeps her prominently in the picture as a horse who can race close to the pace and sustain her effort.
runners_data.comment: Eutropia has won three of her last six starts and was runner-up when last seen 32 days ago. Fit and proven over today's trip from stall five, her rounded recent form edges her into our selection, with matching it the main task.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with a solid record on good ground — two wins and five placings from eleven good-ground starts — making him one of the better ground-form profiles in the race; Mason Paetel claims five pounds, which helps with the weights, but the horse needs the pace to truly collapse for hold-up runners to get into this.
runners_data.comment: Bobacious has been a steady if unremarkable midfield sort, a third his best effort in five recent starts but no better than sixth last time. Fit and experienced over today's distance, drawn in stall nine, our rating of 68 makes him more of a makeweight than a threat.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here and the key pace influence in the race; Eve Johnson Houghton is in strong form (7 from 31 in 14 days), though the style-fit flag suggests Trio may be racing here out of its most comfortable role and should not be assumed to win simply by leading — the 0 wins from 2 runs in similar going tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Trio strung together three creditable thirds before fading to seventh last time out, a fifth the run before, though our rating of 76 still marks her second-best in this field. Seventeen days since that run, drawn in stall seven, the recent dip is the one query.

runners_data.name: Boston Run
runners_data.note: Lightly campaigned sort returning from 194 days off for Simon Dow, which is the dominant flag here — ring rust over such a lay-off over this trip is a significant concern regardless of any tactical consideration; by nature a true hold-up horse, shown in midfield on the map purely because of overcrowding at the rear, so do not read the mapped position as reflecting how Paddy Bradley is likely to ride him.
runners_data.comment: Boston Run's recent form reads modestly, with finishes no better than sixth in his last five starts, including two unplaced efforts. A 194-day layoff is the main concern, though he has experience over today's distance, and drawn in stall two, our rating of 68 keeps him in the frame.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Laughter
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes this three-year-old hard to place tactically; Ed Walker sends out a fair 7 from 42 runner in the 14-day window, but Hurricane Laughter's recent form — all finishes of fifth or worse — and limited good-ground experience (2 from 4 runs) make this a speculative participant at best on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Hurricane Laughter has managed nothing better than fifth in his last four starts, with a well-beaten ninth two starts back the low point. Twenty-seven days since his latest run, with experience over today's distance, drawn in stall four, our rating of 62 leaves him firmly among the outsiders.

runners_data.name: Letsbeatsepsis
runners_data.note: Strong placer on good ground (five placed efforts from eleven starts on this surface) and the tongue tie switch for Gary & Moore is worth noting as a possible gear change; in reality a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield by the map because of the density of closers in this field — Rhys Clutterbuck will likely ride from further back than the map suggests, making a late charge the plan, and the style-fit flag tempers confidence in that materialising cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Letsbeatsepsis rates the outsider of the field on our figures, with nothing better than a second in his last five starts. Fifteen days on, and with the yard having landed with a third of runners in the last fortnight, our rating of 58 still leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Bennyworth
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up racer for Jim Boyle, who has one winner from sixteen recent runners — modest yard form; Sean Bowen's jockeyship adds some confidence in getting a clear run from the back, and a second placing at eight furlongs on standard going is the best recent evidence, though the step up in trip to ten furlongs-plus here is unproven territory for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Bennyworth's form has been modest, with only a second among his last six starts standing out amid four finishes of sixth or worse. Sixteen days since that run, with experience over today's distance, drawn in stall six, our rating of 62 makes him hard to fancy against these.

races.paceDynamic: Trio is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to challenge for the lead, should dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this mile and a half at Epsom. Kitaro Kich and Eutropia are the most likely to press from a prominent position, creating a small lead group but not a truly contested or pressured pace scenario. The hold-up contingent — Penfolds Grange, Bobacious, Bennyworth — will be asked to close from the rear, but with a modest tempo the finishing straight may not stretch far enough for pure closers to reel in those ahead. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to Trio's unhurried pace and pounce once the descent into the Epsom straight begins; note that Boston Run and Letsbeatsepsis are genuine hold-up types pushed into the midfield mapping because the rear is genuinely crowded with closers, and neither is likely to secure the truly prominent berth their redistribution implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trio Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Trio sets a calm, uncontested pace and prominent horses track smoothly before the descent.
scenarios.body: Trio sets the fractions comfortably with Kitaro Kich and Eutropia in tow, and the Epsom hill rewards those who travel well into the straight without burning energy early; horses racing second or third have the clearest run and best vantage point to strike. This shape is the dominant one given the absence of any pace pressure and the tendency for Epsom's downhill finish to suit those already in position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Tempo, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly dawdling early and creates a compressed, bunched straight-line sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With no real pressure on Trio and the field tightly grouped, the faster finishers from midfield can close the gap as the race only truly ignites descending into Tattenham Corner; Penfolds Grange and Bennyworth, both hold-up types with decent form at this trip, are the most likely beneficiaries if they can get a clear run. This outcome requires genuine tactical luck in running for the closers and a tempo slow enough to negate Trio's ability to control the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Kitaro Kich or Eutropia force the issue turning for home, lifting the tempo sharply.
scenarios.body: Should either prominent runner make a decisive move rounding the top bend, the race breaks apart earlier than Trio would prefer and demands stamina rather than finishing speed; a horse like Eutropia, who has proven winning form over a mile and a quarter on firmer surfaces, is well placed to sustain a longer run to the line if the race is set alight from three furlongs out. Trio risks being swallowed up if it cannot respond, and the hold-up horses are likely too far back to capitalise in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues and a truly compressed field produce a messy, incident-strewn straight.
scenarios.body: With several genuine hold-up types shuffled into the midfield and a slow early pace bringing the field together, the Epsom straight can produce a chaotic scramble with horses switching wide and momentum lost in traffic; in such a scenario horses drawn wide or ridden by experienced jockeys navigating the camber — Oisin Murphy on Penfolds Grange notably — hold an edge in getting a clean run. This is the least predictable outcome and carries real risk of interference affecting the result.

watchPoints.text: Trio has sole front-running responsibility but carries a STYLE_FIT flag — monitor whether Callum Hutchinson actually sends forward from the gates or whether a slow break turns the pace dynamic entirely on its head.

Boston Run returns from 194 days off the track; if Simon Dow has been unable to get a racecourse gallop into this horse, significant ring rust over this trip could see it drop away quickly on the descent.

With Letsbeatsepsis and Boston Run both true hold-up types redistributed into midfield, the inside rail in the Epsom straight could become dangerously congested — watch for traffic trouble affecting multiple closers simultaneously.

Eutropia's trainer Adrian Wintle has two winners from eight runners in the 14-day window — a yard in form is worth tracking, and if Tom Marquand is able to position just off Trio's shoulder, Eutropia could be the horse that dictates the finish.

The going is officially unknown at Epsom — any late going stick reading that shifts toward good-to-firm would disproportionately benefit Bobacious, who holds the strongest identical-going record in this field with two wins and five places from eleven such starts.

races.name: Chantilly Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Ian Williams, Greatrex aboard, with three runs on Good or similar going returning 0 wins and 0 places from 9 comparable efforts — the form line and going stats make this a difficult profile to get excited about off a 32-day break.
runners_data.comment: Tiger was runner-up last time out and has finished no worse than 6th in his last five starts, without a win but competitive throughout; he returns from a 32-day break with prior form over today's distance and tops our rating, with the level after the gap his only query.

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied, and the yard fires at 1/5 in the last 14 days — a rare live runner signal — but this horse is a true hold-up type that will likely find itself racing in front of where it wants to be, diluting its ability to deliver the sharp late rattle it needs.
runners_data.comment: Show Biz Kid won two starts back but has been below that level since, finishing 5th last time out; he's fit again after just 28 days with form over today's distance, though he rates only fourth of five in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Perfect Scoundrel
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter with Robert Havlin, whose trainer Perrett has been quiet at 0/5 in the last 14 days; showed a runner-up on Good ground 14 days ago and will be allowed to control matters unchallenged, which is both his asset and potential vulnerability against closers if he wastes energy early.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Scoundrel was runner-up last time out, his best form in his last five starts, and returns quickly just 14 days later with prior form over today's distance; he's without a win and has had some moderate efforts further back, but ranks third of five on our figures.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Has won twice from 15 similar-going efforts including a recent win, and Jack Mitchell partners a horse that will be pushed forward from its natural hold-up position into a midfield role — the redistribution is worth noting context, but the form on comparable ground is genuinely encouraging and the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, Hello Cotai won two starts back and returns after just 15 days with form over today's distance, though he is rated bottom of this five-runner field.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Three-year-old wearing blinkers, most recent run a win over this trip on Good ground 20 days ago, and Tom Marquand takes the ride for a stable that has gone 0/11 in the last fortnight — the trainer stat is a concern, and this horse will be required to make ground from the rear against rivals that may not set a tempo fast enough to suit a pure closer.
runners_data.comment: Booziebrunch won last time out and has never finished worse than 4th in his last five starts, a picture of consistency; he's fit again just 20 days on with form over today's distance, and rates the leading threat here as our second-highest on figures.

races.paceDynamic: Perfect Scoundrel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and will stride out from the gates to set a controlled, uncontested pace over 1m2f on Good turf at Chantilly. With no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, the tempo is likely to be modest and metronomic, favouring a horse that can sit close to the action and pounce in the straight rather than one forced to make up ground from far back. Tiger and Booziebrunch are genuine hold-up types who will be racing from the rear, and while Hello Cotai and Show Biz Kid are also natural hold-up horses, the field contains more hold-up types than can genuinely fill those positions — both have been mapped to midfield and are likely to end up racing slightly closer than usual, with Hello Cotai, given her recent course-form profile, the more likely of the two to actually secure a prominent berth. This shape — a lone leader on a sustainable gallop — most favours a prominent or just-off-the-pace profile that can track Perfect Scoundrel through the race and strike when the pace is wound up in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Scoundrel dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-scorching gallop and the closers cannot generate the sustained late surge needed to peg back the front rank.
scenarios.body: Perfect Scoundrel sets a rhythm from flag to finish that suits a horse tracking in second or third, with Hello Cotai — racing closer than her natural style — ideally placed to exploit the steady tempo; the lack of pace pressure means the leader or a close tracker avoids the extravagant expenditure that would expose a chaser.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle mile to set up a fast-finishing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Tiger or Booziebrunch, racing off the back of the field, would need a searching gallop to create the energy deficit that allows them to reel in the front rank; given there is only one genuine front-runner and no pressure on him, this scenario is conditional on Perfect Scoundrel going off quicker than his style suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Scoundrel steals a decisive break at the top of the straight and the field lacks the finishing kick to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Robert Havlin times the move to stretch his advantage in the final two furlongs, and with a small five-runner field offering little tactical complexity, the uncontested lead gives Perfect Scoundrel the energy reserves to run creditably to the line; his recent runner-up on Good ground gives some encouragement, though trainer Amanda Perrett's 0/5 in the last 14 days is a mild dampener.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes tactical and slow enough in the early stages that Show Biz Kid or Hello Cotai find themselves racing in a genuinely competitive midfield that rewards their remapped position.
scenarios.body: Both horses are true hold-up types racing out of their natural role, so their chance in this shape is discounted by their redistribution; should the race crawl, however, the compressed field could neutralise the advantage of the confirmed front-runner and allow a strong late effort from close quarters.

watchPoints.text: Perfect Scoundrel — watch whether Robert Havlin allows him to coast at a crawl in front; if the gallop is too slow, the hold-up horses behind may arrive with more in the tank than his lone-leader position can handle.

Hello Cotai — monitor how quickly Jack Mitchell sends her forward from the gates; if she secures a position tracking Perfect Scoundrel in second or third, her form on comparable ground becomes highly relevant.

Show Biz Kid — blinkers and a 1/5 trainer strike rate in 14 days are legitimate live flags, but watch whether Dylan Hogan can find a position that allows the horse to close rather than being trapped in an unnatural midfield role.

Booziebrunch — Tom Marquand will be looking for a strong pace that never materialises in this race shape; watch whether the three-year-old can overcome a likely slow tempo from the rear given the trainer's cold recent form.

Field size — with only five runners and one front-runner, the race is at risk of an unusually slow early pace; any significant dawdling through the first half-mile would compress the field and reduce the advantage of positional placement.

races.name: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap Stakes (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course-relevant profile at 1m2f on Good ground; five-year-old in good nick (34 days since last run), trainer Jim Boyle hits 1 from 16 in the past fortnight but the recent form string of 624-37 is inconsistent — this is a natural front-proximity horse who will look to sit just off the lead.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel I
runners_data.note: Massive OR=120 at the head of the weights and confirmed front-runner who will lead, but the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] tag marks her as racing out of her true role; trainer Gihan Arnolda is 1 from 4 in the last 14 days and her recent runs over extreme distances (20f, 17f) suggest this 1m4f trip may not maximise her stamina.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type — not redistributed — whose three-race record on Good ground shows consistency without a win; trainer Jamie Osborne is warm (2 from 16 in 14 days) and the step up to 1m4f looks fine, but she needs a true gallop to deliver her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Authentic hold-up horse who has been knocking on the door over 14-16f on Good ground (three top-four finishes in last five), though never quite winning; trainer Gary & Josh Moore are very active (7 from 21), making this one to track if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Green Team
runners_data.note: Hold-up stayer whose entire recent history is on Tapeta/Standard — zero comparable Good-turf runs in the form book, making the going/surface switch the overriding concern; the recent form of 462441 shows consistency but all of it comes from an artificial surface.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Career record of 12 runs on Good ground from 15 total tells its own story — this is a horse built for this surface; trainer James Owen is in strong form (9 from 46 over 14 days) and the two wins and six places at around 1m4f on Good are directly relevant, making High Fibre one of the better-qualified animals in the field.

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: The form (4-8524) shows a horse capable of placing at this level, and trainer Alan King has firepower — but this runner is a genuine prominent type pushed into the midfield map position because there are simply too many pace horses; jockey Miss Georgia King carries a 5lb claim and the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] rating reflects the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Jodhpur Blue
runners_data.note: An honest, consistent placer (232262) who is a true hold-up type repositioned in the pace map; trainer Ian Williams is busy and solid (4 from 35 in 14 days), and the five-year-old's Good-ground running is limited, though the stamina for 1m4f looks adequate — the [STYLE_FIT=0.91] caveat is the key discount here.

runners_data.name: Naval Command
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (not redistributed) with a limited but usable Good-ground profile (3 from 6); Ralph Beckett's yard is very active (14 from 48 in 14 days) and jockey Miss Georgie Benson claims 7lb, which is a significant weight advantage, though the OR=78 and a form string ending in 9 require improvement.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with decent Good-ground exposure but a form string (144350) that tails off recently and includes a 13th on Good; trainer James Owen also saddles High Fibre, and the head-to-head stable comparison favours that rival given the superior sim-going record — No Knee Never's win-rate over this surface (0 from 6) is a concern.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: The standout form case: four wins in the last five starts, including three consecutive victories, and a 7 from 15 record on sim-going with three wins — the profile screams confidence; jockey Miss Sarah Bowen, trainer Tony Carroll (3 from 42 over 14 days), and a return to Good ground on which she has excelled make this the horse most squarely in the crosshairs of any prominent-running scenario.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: 152 days off the track is the immediate red flag; a genuine hold-up type shifted out of position in the map due to field congestion, and the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] discount compounds the layoff concern — trainer Archie Watson is 0 from 21 in the last 14 days and the Tapeta-heavy recent history (four Standard runs) adds further doubt about immediate readiness on Good turf.

races.paceDynamic: Damascus Steel I is the only confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, critically, she is racing out of her natural role — her [STYLE_FIT=0.93] tag signals she is unlikely to replicate her best form from this position, yet she will still set the fractions and control tempo from the front in the absence of any challenger. With High Fibre, Carnival Day, No Knee Never, and Pride Of Nepal all genuine prominent types, the early order will be organised behind Damascus Steel I but not chaotic — this should produce a measured, sustainable gallop over 1m4f on what is currently an unknown Epsom surface. The field holds more prominent types than the shape can accommodate: I'd Go Maniac is a natural front-runner redistributed to midfield, and Shahbaz and Jodhpur Blue are true hold-up horses also pushed off their natural rear positions — none of these three should be trusted to reproduce their best form, with Pride Of Nepal and High Fibre best placed to genuinely occupy a prominent berth. A controlled, single-pace gallop on this flat mile-and-a-quarter trip strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel in a good position and pick off a fading leader in the final two furlongs — horses with course-relevant stamina and a rhythm of finishing are the profile to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race only quickens in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Damascus Steel I's leadership goes unchallenged, meaning energy is conserved across the field and the race becomes a sprint finish from a long way out; prominent types who travel smoothly and have a turn of foot in the closing stages are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine prominent racers secure their natural position and the pace lifts enough to string the field out from two furlongs down.
scenarios.body: Pride Of Nepal's recent hat-trick of wins and High Fibre's strong Good-ground record at 1m4f make them the key beneficiaries if the gallop has enough substance to expose the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I's front-running draws the pace-prominent types into a faster-than-expected gallop and creates a true end-to-end test.
scenarios.body: Galactic Jack and Epictetus — genuine hold-up horses who are not redistributed — would be the natural late beneficiaries if the race genuinely burns up; Naval Command also gets a mention given her hold-up profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays slower than expected and Damascus Steel I crawls, creating a bunched, lottery-style finish.
scenarios.body: In a crawl-and-sprint scenario the form book counts for less, but horses drawn or positioned to switch out widest into the straight have an edge; Pride Of Nepal's winning habit and Carnival Day's placing record make them natural candidates even in a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Pride Of Nepal has won four of her last five including three on the spin — watch whether she secures a genuinely prominent pitch at the start, because if she does her recent form makes her the most dangerous horse in the race.
High Fibre has run 12 of 15 races on Good ground with two wins and six places at this trip — if the pace is sustainable rather than false, her profile is almost perfectly tailored to this race shape.

Damascus Steel I's OR=120 towers over this field but she is racing out of her optimal role ([STYLE_FIT=0.93]); watch whether her gallop is genuinely searching or if she crawls and sets up a sprint finish that her rivals, not she, can exploit.

Shahbaz's 152-day absence combined with a Tapeta-heavy prep and a [STYLE_FIT=0.92] redistribution means she faces compounded risks — if she shows freshness and bids to get her natural position early, she could cause interference in a bunched early order.

Green Team has never run on Good turf in any of her last five starts — every one was on Standard/Tapeta — making her a genuine surface unknown despite her consistent recent form, and worth monitoring in the betting as market moves here will be largely speculative.

races.name: Vail Williams Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: Form shows a win at 7f on soft and a placed effort on good — Tom Marquand rides and the sim-going record (1W5P) is solid, but as a genuine hold-up horse needing a strong pace to land a blow, this race shape is less than ideal with only Atmosphere in front.|
runners_data.comment: Musical Angel won four starts back but her form has since dipped, including a 6th last time out; she has prior form over today's distance, is fit again after a 15-day break, and our rating still keeps her right among the leading fancies here.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's runner has won at 7f on good going and posted a recent placed run — Sean Levey is a strong booking, and the tongue-plate is noted; like Musical Angel this is a natural hold-up type, and it needs a brisk enough tempo to reel in the front-runners at Epsom.|
runners_data.comment: Cherry Cobbler tops our rating and was runner-up on his latest start. A winner three starts back, he is clearly capable on his day despite some well-beaten efforts further back, the only question being which version of him turns up.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Mischief
runners_data.note: 166-day absence is a significant fitness concern, and while Amanda Perrett's five runners in 14 days is noted, this horse arrives cold; a natural closer by inclination, it has been mapped to midfield due to field congestion at the rear, so it will not be racing in its ideal position and the style-fit discount (0.92) applies.|
runners_data.comment: A winner earlier in his form and returning to a trip he has handled before, Dream Of Mischief ran a solid second last time; the obvious worry is a 166-day absence since, though he retains form over today's distance to fall back on.

runners_data.name: Atmosphere
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's four-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and holds the key tactical advantage — Oisin Murphy can control fractions from the front; the visor is worn, the horse steps back from 8f to 7f, and its stable hit rate in 14 days (1/19) is modest, but race control is a genuine asset here.|
runners_data.comment: Atmosphere has been placed in each of his last five starts, including two runner-up efforts in his last two runs, a picture of consistency; the drawback is a 99-day absence since that run, though he ranks third of five on our figures with prior form over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's runner won at 7f on soft and was placed on good, and Kaiya Fraser takes over the ride with a reasonable 14-day trainer record (2/14); the most likely horse to press Atmosphere for the early lead, it is well drawn to get a prominent position and the drop back from longer trips looks positive.|
runners_data.comment: Uppercase won last time out, ending a mixed run that also included a 9th and 7th further back, and has prior form over today's distance after a 35-day break; even so, he rates only fifth of five in this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Atmosphere is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Uppercase likely to push forward alongside, this is a race where the pace is controlled rather than contested — Oisin Murphy can dictate a sustainable gallop over Epsom's seven furlongs without being pressured into going faster than suits. Uppercase may track in second, but neither horse figures to ignite a genuine speed duel, meaning the tempo could be modest enough to set up a race that rewards tactical positioning rather than pure finishing kick. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape accommodates: Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler are genuine closers, Dream Of Mischief is also a natural hold-up horse but has been redistributed into midfield on the map because there are too many back-markers to place accurately. With a single front-runner setting a controlled pace and no genuine pressure from behind, the race shape favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can sit close to the pace and pounce in the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who need a strong gallop to deliver their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Atmosphere Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Atmosphere dictates a comfortable fractions-driven race and no rival quickens from distance to overwhelm the leaders.
scenarios.body: Murphy sets a fair but unflustered tempo from the front, with Uppercase sitting close enough to pounce; horses comfortable racing on the pace into the Epsom straight are best positioned to benefit as genuine closers lack the strong gallop they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Peg Back Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Atmosphere goes quicker than anticipated and the honest gallop brings the hold-up horses into play late.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would see Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler, both proven at the trip on good going, get competitive ground in the final furlong; Cherry Cobbler's win at 7f on good gives it the strongest form qualification for this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a moderate pace and Dream Of Mischief, though operating out of preferred role, finds an uncontested run through the field.
scenarios.body: Dream Of Mischief's natural hold-up style is compromised by redistribution and a 166-day absence, but its single-figure sim-going record at the trip on standard going shows ability to compete when conditions align; the concern over fitness after such a layoff limits confidence significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Swamps Field
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that the field concertinas and a late burst from a genuine closer overwhelms the front-runners in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given only one horse sets the tempo and Epsom's downhill run naturally encourages front-runners to extend; Musical Angel, who won at 7f on soft going, is the most obvious candidate if this unlikely scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: Atmosphere's ability to control fractions without being pushed by Uppercase is the race's defining factor — watch whether Murphy settles into a genuine rhythm or is forced to quicken earlier than ideal.

Dream Of Mischief returns from a 166-day absence and has been mapped out of its natural hold-up position; monitor whether it actually races closer to the pace or drops right away, as either outcome affects the race shape materially.

Cherry Cobbler and Musical Angel are both natural closers and need a strong gallop to fire — if the tempo is modest, watch for them to get outpaced entering the Epsom straight with too much ground to make up.

Uppercase's opening move is worth tracking — if it pushes Atmosphere hard for the lead it could inject pace that transforms this into a more genuinely-run race and brings the hold-up horses back into contention.

races.name: Betfred Everswift 30 July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Ollie Sangster and Hector Crouch with solid recent form (three consecutive placings), handles good ground well based on hist, and at 7f on good turf at Epsom the profile stacks up; 17 days since last run is a positive freshness angle.
runners_data.comment: Piazza has been knocking on the door without getting over the line, with two thirds among her last five starts and never worse than fifth. Drawn in stall two on a 17-day turnaround, our rating of 72 makes her the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — five placings in recent starts — yet struggles to convert; good ground form is evidenced (multiple good-ground efforts) but the 32-day absence and Alistair Rawlinson replacing a stronger pilot are mild negatives, and a blinkered run last time produced no improvement.
runners_data.comment: Eyes Front has been the model of consistency, finishing fifth in four of his last five starts and never far away. Thirty-two days on from that run, our rating of 66 keeps him among the leading dangers, though he still needs more to add to those places.

runners_data.name: Mayfair Market
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride for S Woods but this hold-up type has been finishing well down the field recently (form string 45-689 is deteriorating), tongue-tied, and the step back to 7f from 8f is a question mark rather than a clear plus.

runners_data.name: Twilight Glow
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's visor-wearing closer is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map due to field composition; the form (best effort a 4th) and going stats (6/9 runs in similar conditions, zero wins) give little cause for optimism even if it manages to find its natural rhythm from further back.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Glow's form has been up and down, though he improved to sixth last time out having been no better than eighth two starts back. Seventeen days on, our rating of 65 keeps him among the leading dangers, though he needs more again to feature.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's three-year-old is a genuine closer in profile but has been pushed into midfield on the map; Neil Callan's booking is the one positive flag, though 56 days off, limited good-ground form (2/5 in similar going) and a worrying recent run of sixes and eights makes enthusiasm hard to summon.
runners_data.comment: Sun Of Dolly has struggled to threaten, with a fourth two starts back his only look at the frame among five modest starts. A 56-day gap since his last run and our rating of 60 leave him well down the pecking order, drawn in stall seven.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's hold-up type is positioned in midfield on this map because the true rear is overcrowded — Sean Levey is a strong jockey booking and the horse did finish second last time on standard ground, but it has raced predominantly on standard rather than good and the style misfit here is a meaningful concern.
runners_data.comment: Credit Forgedd It's recent form reads fourth, ninth, fifth, second, fifth, with that second four starts back the highlight amid otherwise workmanlike efforts. Sixteen days on, drawn in stall one, our rating of 62 makes him a fair, if unspectacular, midfield type.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: The race's sole pace-setter and the key to how this shapes up — Rachel Cook & John Bridger's runner has shown front-running ability over 6f with two second-place finishes, but stepping up to 7f at Epsom on good turf is an unknown, and apprentice Mason Paetel (5lb claim) adds a slight tactical uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Madman bounced back to finish second last time out, having found only ninth two starts back. A 37-day absence since that run is the obvious query, but drawn in stall five, our rating of 66 marks him second-best in the race and a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking for Richard Spencer is the eye-catching entry here; a true hold-up horse who, crucially, is likely to actually secure a genuine rear berth unlike many rivals in this shape; only 6 days since last run is a minor flag, but a headgear change to hood and a top-tier jockey appointment merit respect.
runners_data.comment: Ice Cube has been a model of consistency without threatening to win, with a third his best effort in his last five starts. Quick to reappear just six days on, drawn in stall four, our rating of 65 keeps him firmly involved without quite standing out.

runners_data.name: Karisma's Angel
runners_data.note: Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark is a classier combination than the OR-57 rating suggests, and the 153-day layoff is the obvious concern — this horse has been off since March, but a second last time on standard ground shows ability; genuinely held up, and like Ice Cube is one of the few who can authentically race from the rear in this field.
runners_data.comment: Karisma's Angel's recent form has been patchy, with a second last time out the one bright spot among a run of modest efforts. Drawn in stall eight, a 153-day absence since that run, and our rating of 57 - the lowest in the field - leave her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Madman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 7f handicap at Epsom and will be allowed to bowl along at the head of affairs unchallenged, creating a controlled, even gallop rather than a true slog. With no genuine rival willing to take him on, the tempo is likely to be fair-to-moderate rather than punishing, which historically at Epsom's undulating 7f suits horses that can travel sweetly in the first half and produce a sustained finish rather than those who need extreme pace to bring them into it. The field is heavily populated with hold-up types — Twilight Glow, Sun Of Dolly, Credit Forgedd It, Ice Cube and Karisma's Angel are all true closers who have been redistributed into midfield slots on the map because they cannot all occupy the rear simultaneously — of those, Ice Cube (Oisin Murphy, freshened up) and Karisma's Angel (Kieran Shoemark, Ed Walker) are most likely to actually secure a rear-group berth, while the others are likely to bunch in mid-division and race somewhat out of their comfort zones. The tactical verdict is clear: a race run at a controlled, uncontested pace over Epsom's quirky 7f layout favours prominent-to-midfield horses with strong sustained finishing ability rather than true sit-and-sprint closers who need a stronger galop to get into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Madman Dictates, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Madman is given a completely unchallenged lead and controls a moderate, even gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Madman sets a comfortable pace, the field fans out behind on the home straight and horses closest to the pace hold a decisive positional advantage at the business end; the controlled tempo means closers face too big a gap to bridge from the rear. Prominent or handy runners who can travel kindly and hit the rising ground in rhythm are the clear beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow quickens early — even fractionally — or the field compresses behind Madman and creates a falsely-run section that bunches the hold-up horses into contention.
scenarios.body: The natural closers in this field are plentiful, and if they can travel unobtrusively in a compact pack before unleashing late runs down Epsom's straight, the hold-up brigade gets its ideal scenario; the key is that the redistribution effect means many of them will be racing slightly wider or more forward than they would prefer. Ice Cube and Karisma's Angel, as the most naturally positioned hold-up horses, are best placed to benefit if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Form Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that the race turns into a stamina-and-class test in the final two furlongs with few clear winners emerging.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race that strings out into the home straight rewards horses with the highest raw ability and best recent form regardless of style; the Epsom camber and undulations begin to sort the field by quality rather than position. Piazza and Eyes Front, both OR 64-65 types with decent recent form figures, could emerge from a muddled contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a runner shows unexpected pace or position and secures an uncontested berth just behind Madman, tracking the leader to the turn and kicking clear.
scenarios.body: This shape relies on a horse racing significantly out of its stated role and besting Madman or a near-leader to the line; it is the least likely outcome given the concentration of hold-up types who cannot all shift dramatically forward. Credit Forgedd It with Sean Levey is the most plausible beneficiary if that positional switch is executed early.

watchPoints.text: Madman's pace judgment is critical — if Mason Paetel (apprentice) goes too fast early over 7f at Epsom the race could turn into a true test and shut the door on all closers; monitor how aggressively Madman is ridden in the opening furlong.

Ice Cube (Oisin Murphy) represents the most significant jockey-upgrade angle in the field — watch the market from opening shows, as Murphy does not take rides in modest 7f handicaps without expectation.

Karisma's Angel returns from 153 days off for Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark — this combination routinely targets first-time-out winners from a break, and the booking at this level is disproportionate to the current OR; bear that in mind if it is supported.

The redistribution of five hold-up horses into midfield means the early part of the race could see significant positional jostling — watch for any of Twilight Glow, Sun Of Dolly or Credit Forgedd It to be caught wide or unable to settle, which would effectively eliminate them.

Epsom's 7f camber and downhill sections reward horses that handle the track; none of these runners has a confirmed Epsom win on record, so course specialists cannot be identified — treat any horse that looks comfortable early in the race as a potential improver.
